key_insight: First-fracture in stretched periodic polymer chains is governed by a chain-coupled free-energy landscape, where barrier growth and dynamical recrossing together set the absolute rate.
engineering_relevance: This provides a rate-predictive framework for polymer fracture and healing that can feed mesoscopic damage models of networks and highly stretched materials.
method: Constrained-partition calculations for intact-chain populations and tensions
Intact-reservoir PMF to estimate first-fracture surface probabilities
Kramers-Grote-Hynes, nonlinear reactive-flux, and quasi-deterministic barrier-top trajectory analysis
evidence_signal: The theoretical rates and populations closely match equilibrium simulations, and several independent rate tests show good agreement up to an operational chain-length limit.
watch_item: Two-state kinetics becomes unreliable for longer chains where healing is too rare and multiple-fracture effects may start to matter, especially beyond coexistence.
paper_title: First-fracture kinetics in periodic chains: from free-energy landscapes and dynamical recrossing to absolute rates
